newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Positive 97 outlook at Villeroy & Boch.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Positive 97 outlook at Villeroy & Boch.

text.p: German tableware and bathroom fittings group Villeroy & Boch AG said on Wednesday that its outlook for the current year was positive, despite reporting losses in calendar 1996.

Villeroy reported a group net loss of 103 million marks ($60.2 million) in 1996, compared to group net profits of 34.1 million marks in 1995, which the group said related to a 114.1 million mark charge in 1996 as part of a restructuring.

The group said it did not expect to face further charges in 1997 or 1998 and that it would start to reap the benefits of its restructuring programme with a "clear profit improvement" for the current business year.

In a regulatory statement, Villeroy said that group income from ordinary activities in 1996 was 33 million marks, down from 87.4 million a year earlier, while group sales in 1996 fell two percent to 1.453 billion marks.
Group said that lower sales in its bathroom fittings unit and losses in its tiles unit had a negative effect, but that it expected problems in these areas to be resolved by 1998.
Villeroy's tableware unit managed to report slightly higher earnings last year, despite difficult market conditions, the statement said.
All market segments increased their market share during the year, Villeroy said.
The group's capital-to-assets ratio fell to 36.9 percent from 42.6 percent because of the losses.
Villeroy has previously said it would not pay a dividend on its 1996 results. Its dividend payout in 1995 was 7.50 marks per preference share and 6.50 marks per ordinary share.
The group said its products were well-received at international trade fairs in early 1997 and that its tableware and tiles groups reported higher sales in the first quarter over year-ago levels.
